high dose ascorbate administration does not normalize renal haemodynamics in normoalbuminic, normotensive IDDM patients.
the administration of high dose AA to normoalbuminuriac IDDM patients did not change the renal haemodynamics.

the study of the effects of the high dose ascorbate (AA) on the kidney in normoalbumuric IDDM.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

high doses of AA do not affect the renal hemodynamic parameters of GFR, ERPF, FF and renal blood flow (RBF), in normoalbuminic IDDM patients, and that this is not due to any change in the renal vascular resistance (RVR).
high dose AA does not normalize glomerular haemodynamics in normoalbumiuric, normotenive, male IDDM patients.
high doses of AA do not normalize glomerular haemodynamics in normoalbuminaemic, normotensive, male IDDM patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the following: (1) that AA is not an effective treatment for diabetic nephropathy; (2) that it is safe and well tolerated in doses of 6 grams twice a day; and (3) that AA does not have any significant effect on renal hemodynamics, including the glomerular filtration fraction, in normoalbuminic, normotensive IDDM patients.
the results of this study do not support the hypothesis that AA has a renoprotective effect in IDDM patients.
high dose AA does not have a significant effect on glomerular hyper-filtration in normoalbuminu-ric IDDM patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of high dose vitamin C are not as dramatic as the media would lead us to believe.
the use of a single high dose of vitamin C is not effective in improving renal function in people with diabetes.
the use of a high dose of ascorbic acid is a promising approach to the treatment of glomerular hyperperfusion in IDDM patients, and may have a role in the prevention of diabetic nephropathy.
